relations.rationale: These describe different activities during lunch and neither implies the other.
Isla checking on progress has no bearing on whether Vik enjoyed the competition most.
Sami helping fix a loose axle sets up the context where the axle could pop off again, making the second event more plausible.
Helping fix an axle earlier is unrelated to the later group activity of packing away tools.
The noise of servo motors and clapping filling the room is consistent with and suggests teams racing machines, supporting that event.
Teams racing is the competitive event that would let Vik seem to enjoy the competition, supporting that claim.
Racing machines down the corridor is the scenario in which Vik's robot could inch ahead and he'd grin, supporting this claim.
Racing establishes the context for ranking speed, supporting the possibility that Kai ranked fastest.
Racing earlier is a separate event from the later packing away of tools, with no direct implication either way.
Racing during the day doesn't specifically imply anything about future plans being discussed.
Vik enjoying the competition most is consistent with and supports the detail that he grinned when his robot advanced.
Vik's enjoyment of the competition doesn't specifically relate to the group discussing the next session.
Vik grinning when ahead doesn't imply anything about the overall agreement on how small the speed difference was.
Vik's grinning during competition is unrelated to the later packing away of tools.
Kai ranking fastest overall is compatible with the difference in speed still being small, so it supports rather than contradicts.
Agreement on speed differences has no clear connection to talk about the next session.
Packing away tools and sweeping the floor together are both part of winding down, so one supports the plausibility of the other happening concurrently.
Packing away tools as the workshop wound down is consistent with and supports the group starting to talk about the next session.
Sweeping the floor together as the workshop wound down supports the idea that the group was already discussing the next session.
